title: CUET General Test Test 6
subject: General Test (Code: 501)
syllabus_source: CUET SYLLABUS/General Test - 501.pdf (NTA syllabus for CUET (UG) 2026, latest published)
past_paper_reference: Pattern benchmark only: CUET (UG) 2025 and 2026 General Test shift analyses (no questions copied)

instructions: Each correct answer earns 5 marks; each incorrect answer deducts 1 mark; unattempted questions earn 0.
The last 5 questions are a data-interpretation set based on one table; the set stays together.

questions.sub_topic: Actual time from a mirror image of a clock
questions.question: A clock seen in a mirror appears to show 4:30. What is the actual time?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 7:30
Answer steps: for a mirror image, actual time = 11:60 − time seen = 11:60 − 4:30 = 7:30.
Why not the others: (B) subtracts from 12:60. (C) subtracts from 10:60. (D) assumes a mirror does not change the time.
Key point: Mirror image + actual time = 12:00 (for times between 1:00 and 11:00).

questions.sub_topic: Statements about acids and bases
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about acids and bases:
A. Acids turn red litmus blue.
B. Bases turn phenolphthalein solution pink.
C. Milk of magnesia, used as an antacid, is a base.
D. An acid and a base react to form a salt and water.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B and D only
C) B, C and D only
D) A, B, C and D
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) B, C and D only
Why: B is correct: phenolphthalein is colourless in acids and pink in bases. C is correct: milk of magnesia (magnesium hydroxide) neutralises excess stomach acid. D is correct: this is neutralisation.
Why not the others: A is wrong: acids turn blue litmus red; bases turn red litmus blue. Options (A), (B) and (D) include A.
Key point: Acid — blue litmus to red; base — red litmus to blue.

questions.sub_topic: Syllogism of books, pages and pens
questions.question:
Statements:
All books are pages.
No page is a pen.
Conclusions:
I. No book is a pen.
II. Some pages are books.
Which of the conclusions follow?
options: C) Both I and II follow
D) Neither I nor II follows
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Both I and II follow
Answer steps: every book lies inside "pages", and no page is a pen, so no book can be a pen (I). Since all books are pages, some pages are books (II).
Why not the others: (A) and (B) each miss one certain conclusion. (D) rejects both.
Key point: "All A are B" + "No B is C" gives "No A is C".

questions.sub_topic: Number pattern from sums of squares
questions.question: If 2 × 3 = 13, 3 × 4 = 25 and 4 × 5 = 41, then 5 × 6 = ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 61
Answer steps: in each case the result is the sum of the squares: 2² + 3² = 13, 3² + 4² = 25, 4² + 5² = 41. So 5 × 6 = 5² + 6² = 25 + 36 = 61.
Why not the others: (B) is the ordinary product. (C) and (D) follow no rule that fits all three examples.
Key point: Test a rule on every example given, not just the first.

questions.sub_topic: Date of World Environment Day
questions.question: World Environment Day, led by the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), is observed every year on:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 5 June
Why: World Environment Day has been observed on 5 June since 1973, marking the opening of the Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment (5 June 1972).
Why not the others: (A) is Earth Day. (C) is the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer. (D) is World Water Day.
Key point: 5 June — Environment; 22 April — Earth; 16 September — Ozone.

questions.sub_topic: Rocket that launched CMS-03
questions.question: Which rocket launched CMS-03, the heaviest communication satellite (about 4,410 kg) launched from Indian soil, on 2 November 2025?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) LVM3
Why: CMS-03, a multi-band communication satellite for the Indian Navy, was placed in a geosynchronous transfer orbit by LVM3-M5 from Sriharikota. LVM3, nicknamed "Bahubali", is ISRO's heaviest rocket.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) carry much lighter loads, mostly to low orbits. (D) can lift only about 2,250 kg to a transfer orbit.
Key point: LVM3 also launched Chandrayaan-3 (2023).

questions.sub_topic: Speed of light in a vacuum
questions.question: What is the approximate speed of light in a vacuum?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 3 × 10⁸ m/s
Why: Light travels at about 3 × 10⁸ metres per second (300,000 km/s) in a vacuum.
Why not the others: (B) is 300 km/s, a thousand times too slow (the confusion is between km/s and m/s). (A) is a hundred times too slow. (C) is about the speed of sound in air.
Key point: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach the Earth.

questions.sub_topic: Value of an expression with defined operations
questions.question: If a $ b means a² − b², and a # b means (a + b)², what is the value of (5 $ 3) # 2?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 324
Answer steps: 5 $ 3 = 25 − 9 = 16. Then 16 # 2 = (16 + 2)² = 18² = 324.
Why not the others: (A) gives 16², leaving out the + 2. (B) uses 16 − 2. (D) gives 2 × 144, a slip in squaring 18.
Key point: Work the bracket first, then apply the outer operation to the result.

questions.sub_topic: Statements about the first Kho Kho World Cup
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Kho Kho World Cup held in January 2025:
A. It was the first Kho Kho World Cup.
B. It was held in New Delhi.
C. India won only the women's title.
D. Nepal were the runners-up in both the men's and women's finals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B and C only
C) B, C and D only
D) A, B and D only
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) A, B and D only
Why: A and B are correct: the first edition was held at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, New Delhi, from 13 to 19 January 2025. D is correct: India beat Nepal in both finals (women 78–40, men 54–36) on 19 January.
Why not the others: C is wrong: India won both the women's and the men's titles. Options (B) and (C) include C; (A) leaves out the correct statement D.
Key point: Kho Kho is an Indian tag game played by two teams of 12 (9 take the field).

questions.sub_topic: Series of cubes plus two
questions.question: Find the next number: 3, 10, 29, 66, 127, ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 218
Answer steps: the terms are 1³ + 2, 2³ + 2, 3³ + 2, 4³ + 2, 5³ + 2, so the next is 6³ + 2 = 218.
Why not the others: (A) is 6³ without the +2. (B) subtracts 2. (C) adds 4.
Key point: Compare each term with the nearest square or cube.

questions.sub_topic: Speed of the stream from upstream and downstream times
questions.question: A boat goes 30 km upstream in 6 hours and the same distance downstream in 3 hours. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 2.5 km/h
Given: upstream speed = 30 ÷ 6 = 5 km/h; downstream speed = 30 ÷ 3 = 10 km/h.
Step 1: Speed of the stream = (downstream − upstream) ÷ 2 = (10 − 5) ÷ 2 = 2.5 km/h.
Step 2: (The boat's speed in still water is (10 + 5) ÷ 2 = 7.5 km/h.)
Common mistake: giving the boat's speed (7.5 km/h, option A), or forgetting to halve the difference (5 km/h, option B).

questions.sub_topic: Disease caused by a virus
questions.question: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Polio
Why: Polio is caused by the poliovirus, which spreads through contaminated food and water. India was declared polio-free by the WHO in 2014.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) are caused by bacteria (Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Salmonella typhi). (B) is caused by a protozoan (Plasmodium) spread by female Anopheles mosquitoes.
Key point: Antibiotics work against bacteria, not viruses.

questions.sub_topic: Mother's age from a past multiple
questions.question: The sum of the present ages of a mother and her daughter is 50 years. Five years ago, the mother was 7 times as old as the daughter. What is the mother's present age?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 40 years
Given: M + D = 50; M − 5 = 7(D − 5).
Step 1: M = 50 − D, so 45 − D = 7D − 35.
Step 2: 8D = 80, D = 10; M = 40.
Step 3: Check: five years ago, 35 = 7 × 5.
Common mistake: giving the mother's age five years ago (35, option A) or the daughter's age (10, option D).

questions.sub_topic: Solving two linear equations
questions.question: If 2x − 3y = 7 and x + y = 6, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 5
Given: 2x − 3y = 7 and x + y = 6.
Step 1: Multiply the second equation by 3: 3x + 3y = 18.
Step 2: Add to the first: 5x = 25, so x = 5 (and y = 1).
Common mistake: giving the value of y (1, option A).

questions.sub_topic: Odd one out among metals and an alloy
questions.question: Choose the one that does not belong with the others: Copper, Iron, Brass, Aluminium
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Brass
Answer steps: copper, iron and aluminium are elements (pure metals). Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are all elements.
Key point: Alloys are mixtures of metals, such as brass, bronze and steel.

questions.sub_topic: Subject of the 2025 Nobel Prize in Medicine
questions.question: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, awarded to Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell and Shimon Sakaguchi, was for discoveries about:
options: A) Regulatory T cells and immune tolerance
C) MicroRNA and the control of genes
D) Gene editing with the CRISPR tool
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Regulatory T cells and immune tolerance
Why: The prize, announced on 6 October 2025, honoured their work on how regulatory T cells and the Foxp3 gene stop the immune system from attacking the body's own tissues.
Why not the others: (B) won the 2023 Medicine prize (Karikó and Weissman). (C) won the 2024 Medicine prize (Ambros and Ruvkun). (D) won the 2020 Chemistry prize (Charpentier and Doudna).
Key point: The work could help in treating autoimmune diseases and cancer, and in organ transplants.

questions.sub_topic: Monuments in the order they were built
questions.question:
Arrange the following monuments in the order in which they were built (earliest first):
A. Taj Mahal
B. Victoria Memorial
C. Qutub Minar
D. Charminar
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) C, D, A, B
Why: Qutub Minar, Delhi (begun about 1199 by Qutb-ud-din Aibak); Charminar, Hyderabad (1591, Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah); Taj Mahal, Agra (about 1632–1653, Shah Jahan); Victoria Memorial, Kolkata (1906–1921).
Why not the others: (A) puts the Taj Mahal before the Charminar. (B) starts with the Charminar. (D) puts the Victoria Memorial before the Taj Mahal.
Key point: About 1200, 1591, 1632–53, 1906–21.

questions.sub_topic: Birthday months of five friends
questions.question: The birthdays of five friends A, B, C, D and E fall in February, April, June, August and October, one in each month. C's birthday is in June. Exactly one friend's birthday falls between A's and C's. B's birthday comes in the month just after D's. E's birthday is not in February. A's birthday comes after E's. Whose birthday is in August?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) E
Answer steps: number the months 1 to 5 (February to October); C is 3. A is 1 or 5. If A were 1 (February), E would have to come before A, which is impossible. So A is 5 (October). D and B must be next to each other with B after D: only 1–2 is free, so D is February and B is April. E takes August.
Why not the others: (A) D is in February. (C) A is in October. (D) B is in April.
Key point: Test both places for the person with two choices and keep the one that fits every clue.

questions.sub_topic: Gain from selling cloth when profit equals selling price of part
questions.question: By selling 33 metres of cloth, a shopkeeper gains the selling price of 11 metres. What is his gain percentage?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 50%
Given: SP of 33 m − CP of 33 m = SP of 11 m.
Step 1: So CP of 33 m = SP of 22 m.
Step 2: Gain on the cost of 22 m of selling price is the price of 11 m: gain % = 11 ÷ 22 × 100 = 50%.
Common mistake: dividing 11 by 33 (33.33%, option B); the gain must be compared with the cost, which equals the selling price of 22 m.

questions.sub_topic: Author of the Arthashastra
questions.question: Who wrote the "Arthashastra", an ancient treatise on statecraft and economics?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Kautilya
Why: The Arthashastra is traditionally credited to Kautilya (also called Chanakya or Vishnugupta), adviser to Chandragupta Maurya.
Why not the others: (B) wrote "Abhijnanashakuntalam" and "Meghaduta". (C), a Greek envoy at the Mauryan court, wrote "Indica". (D) wrote "Harshacharita".
Key point: Arthashastra — Kautilya; Indica — Megasthenes.

questions.sub_topic: Lakes and their states
questions.question:
Match the lakes in List-I with the state or Union Territory in which they lie in List-II:

List-I
(A) Chilika Lake
(B) Loktak Lake
(C) Wular Lake
(D) Sambhar Lake

List-II
(I) Rajasthan
(II) Jammu and Kashmir
(III) Manipur
(IV) Odisha
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Chilika — Odisha, India's largest brackish-water lagoon (IV); Loktak — Manipur, with floating islands called phumdis (III); Wular — Jammu and Kashmir, one of Asia's largest freshwater lakes (II); Sambhar — Rajasthan, India's largest inland salt lake (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Chilika and Loktak; (C) swaps Loktak and Wular; (D) swaps Wular and Sambhar.
Key point: Keibul Lamjao, on Loktak's phumdis, is the world's only floating national park.

questions.sub_topic: First Indian Governor-General of independent India
questions.question: Who was the first and only Indian Governor-General of independent India?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) C. Rajagopalachari
Why: C. Rajagopalachari ("Rajaji") succeeded Lord Mountbatten in June 1948 and held the office until 26 January 1950, when India became a republic and the post was abolished.
Why not the others: (A) was the first Governor-General of independent India, but he was British. (B) became the first President in 1950. (C) was the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister.
Key point: Rajaji was also one of the first recipients of the Bharat Ratna (1954).

questions.sub_topic: Longest river in Asia
questions.question: Which is the longest river in Asia?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Yangtze
Why: The Yangtze (Chang Jiang), about 6,300 km long, flows across China to the East China Sea near Shanghai. It is the third-longest river in the world.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are all shorter (the Mekong is about 4,900 km; the Ganga about 2,500 km).
Key point: The Three Gorges Dam, on the Yangtze, is the world's largest hydroelectric power station.

questions.sub_topic: Currencies and their countries
questions.question:
Match the currencies in List-I with their countries in List-II:

List-I
(A) Taka
(B) Rand
(C) Ringgit
(D) Real

List-II
(I) Brazil
(II) Malaysia
(III) South Africa
(IV) Bangladesh
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Taka — Bangladesh (IV); Rand — South Africa (III); Ringgit — Malaysia (II); Real — Brazil (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the Taka and the Rand; (C) swaps the Rand and the Ringgit; (D) swaps the Ringgit and the Real.
Key point: Brazil, South Africa and India are all members of BRICS; their currencies are the real, the rand and the rupee.

questions.sub_topic: Fourth proportional to three numbers
questions.question: What is the fourth proportional to 4, 9 and 12?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 27
Given: 4 : 9 = 12 : x.
Step 1: 4x = 9 × 12 = 108.
Step 2: x = 27.
Common mistake: setting it up as 4 : 12 = 9 : x without care for order (also 27 here), or multiplying 9 by 4 (36, option B) instead of solving the proportion.

questions.sub_topic: Probability of drawing a king or a heart
questions.question: A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of 52 playing cards. What is the probability that it is a king or a heart?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 4/13
Given: 4 kings and 13 hearts; one card (the king of hearts) is both.
Step 1: Favourable cards = 4 + 13 − 1 = 16.
Step 2: Probability = 16/52 = 4/13.
Common mistake: counting the king of hearts twice (17/52, option A), or counting only hearts (1/4, option B) or only kings (1/13, option D).

questions.sub_topic: City of the first G20 summit in Africa
questions.question: The G20 Leaders' Summit of 22–23 November 2025, the first G20 summit held in Africa, took place in which city?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Johannesburg
Why: South Africa held the G20 presidency from 1 December 2024 and hosted the summit at the Johannesburg Expo Centre, the first time the group's leaders met on the African continent.
Why not the others: (A) is South Africa's legislative capital but not the venue. (B) and (D) are in Kenya and Egypt, which are not G20 members.
Key point: The African Union became a permanent member of the G20 at the New Delhi summit in 2023.

questions.sub_topic: Why lightning is seen before thunder is heard
questions.question:
Assertion (A): During a storm, we see the flash of lightning before we hear the thunder.
Reason (R): Light travels much faster than sound.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both are true. The flash and the thunder are produced at the same moment, but light (about 3 × 10⁸ m/s) reaches us almost at once, while sound (about 340 m/s in air) takes about 3 seconds per kilometre. So (R) explains (A).
Why not the others: (B) denies the link. (C) and (D) call a true statement false.
Key point: Counting the seconds between the flash and the thunder and dividing by 3 gives the distance of the storm in kilometres.

questions.sub_topic: Global environmental agreements in order
questions.question:
Arrange the following international environmental milestones in chronological order (earliest first):
A. Kyoto Protocol
B. Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment
C. Paris Agreement
D. Montreal Protocol
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) B, D, A, C
Why: Stockholm Conference (1972), Montreal Protocol on ozone-depleting substances (1987), Kyoto Protocol on greenhouse gases (1997) and the Paris Agreement (2015).
Why not the others: (A) puts Kyoto before Montreal. (B) starts with Montreal. (C) puts Paris before Kyoto.
Key point: 1972, 1987, 1997, 2015.

questions.sub_topic: Statements about the Governor of a state
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Governor of a state in India:
A. The Governor is appointed by the President.
B. The minimum age to be appointed Governor is 30 years.
C. The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President.
D. The same person can be appointed Governor of two or more states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: B) A, B and C only
C) B, C and D only
D) A, C and D only
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) A, C and D only
Why: A is correct (Article 155). C is correct (Article 156). D is correct: the 7th Amendment (1956) allows one person to be Governor of two or more states.
Why not the others: B is wrong: the minimum age is 35 years (Article 157). Options (B) and (C) include B; (A) leaves out the correct statement D.
Key point: The Governor is the constitutional head of a state, as the President is of the Union.

questions.sub_topic: Counting members of a joint family
questions.question: A family has a man, his wife, their three sons with their wives, and two children for each son. How many members are there in the family?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 14
Answer steps: man and wife = 2; three sons and their wives = 6; two children for each son = 6. Total = 2 + 6 + 6 = 14.
Why not the others: (A) forgets the man and his wife. (B) gives each son one child and adds the parents (2 + 6 + 3). (D) counts four children for one son.
Key point: Count each generation separately.

questions.sub_topic: Days needed with fewer workers and longer hours
questions.question: 15 workers, working 8 hours a day, finish a job in 12 days. How many days will 12 workers take to finish the same job working 10 hours a day?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 12 days
Given: work = workers × hours a day × days.
Step 1: Total = 15 × 8 × 12 = 1440 worker-hours.
Step 2: New daily output = 12 × 10 = 120 worker-hours.
Step 3: Days = 1440 ÷ 120 = 12 days.
Common mistake: changing only for the number of workers (15 days, option B) or only for the hours (9.6 days, option C).

questions.sub_topic: Area of a circle from its circumference
questions.question: The circumference of a circle is 44 cm. What is its area? (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 154 cm²
Given: circumference = 2πr = 44 cm.
Step 1: r = 44 ÷ (2 × 22/7) = 7 cm.
Step 2: Area = πr² = 22/7 × 49 = 154 cm².
Common mistake: taking 14 cm (the diameter) as the radius (616 cm², option A).

questions.sub_topic: People who speak only English
questions.question: In a group of 100 people, 72 speak Hindi and 43 speak English. Everyone speaks at least one of the two. How many people speak only English?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 28
Answer steps: both = 72 + 43 − 100 = 15. Only English = 43 − 15 = 28.
Why not the others: (B) counts everyone who speaks English. (C) is the number who speak both. (D) is the number who speak only Hindi.
Key point: Find the overlap first, then subtract it.

questions.sub_topic: Gas released when zinc reacts with an acid
questions.question: Which gas is given off when zinc granules react with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Hydrogen
Why: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. The gas burns with a "pop" sound when a lighted splint is brought near.
Why not the others: (A) relights a glowing splint and is not produced here. (C) is not released because the chlorine stays in zinc chloride. (D) comes from acids reacting with carbonates.
Key point: Active metals + dilute acid → salt + hydrogen.

questions.sub_topic: Aim of the Chipko movement
questions.question: The Chipko movement of the 1970s in the Garhwal Himalaya (now Uttarakhand) was mainly aimed at:
options: A) Stopping the building of large dams
B) Saving rivers from industrial pollution
C) Protecting trees and forests from being cut down
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Protecting trees and forests from being cut down
Why: In 1973, villagers — many of them women, such as Gaura Devi — hugged ("chipko") trees to stop contractors from felling them. Sunderlal Bahuguna and Chandi Prasad Bhatt were among its leaders.
Why not the others: (A) was the aim of the Narmada Bachao Andolan. (B) and (D) were not the aims of Chipko.
Key point: The Appiko movement of Karnataka (1983) was inspired by Chipko.

questions.sub_topic: State with the twelfth Maratha fort on the World Heritage List
questions.question: The "Maratha Military Landscapes of India", inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in July 2025, are 12 forts — 11 in Maharashtra and one in which other state?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Tamil Nadu
Why: The serial site, inscribed on 11 July 2025 at the World Heritage Committee's 47th session in Paris, includes Raigad, Rajgad, Pratapgad, Sindhudurg and other forts in Maharashtra, and Gingee Fort in Tamil Nadu. It became India's 44th World Heritage Site.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) have Maratha-era forts, but none of them is part of this listing.
Key point: India's 43rd site was the Moidams of Charaideo, Assam (2024).

questions.sub_topic: Assumption behind a buy-one-get-one offer
questions.question:
Statement: An advertisement for a new soap says, "Buy one, get one free!"
Assumptions:
I. People are attracted by free offers.
II. The soap is of poor quality.
Which of the assumptions is implicit?
options: B) Both I and II are implicit
C) Neither I nor II is implicit
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Only I is implicit
Answer steps: the advertiser expects the free offer to draw buyers, which assumes people like free offers (I). Nothing in the offer says the soap is poor; companies use such offers to launch new products, so II is not assumed.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) accept II, a negative guess. (C) rejects I, which the offer depends on.
Key point: An advertisement assumes that its message will work on buyers.

questions.sub_topic: Animals and their classes
questions.question:
Match the animals in List-I with the classes they belong to in List-II:

List-I
(A) Frog
(B) Bat
(C) Penguin
(D) Shark

List-II
(I) Fish
(II) Bird
(III) Mammal
(IV) Amphibian
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Frog — amphibian, living in water and on land (IV); bat — mammal, the only mammal capable of true flight (III); penguin — bird that cannot fly (II); shark — fish with a skeleton of cartilage (I).
Why not the others: (B) swaps the frog and the bat; (C) swaps the bat and the penguin; (D) swaps the penguin and the shark.
Key point: Classify animals by their body features, not by where they live or whether they fly.

questions.sub_topic: Direction after the compass is rotated
questions.question: If south-east becomes north, north-east becomes west, and all other directions change in the same way, what will west become?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) South-east
Answer steps: south-east → north is a turn of 135° anticlockwise; north-east → west is also 135° anticlockwise. Turning west by 135° anticlockwise: west → south-west (45°) → south (90°) → south-east (135°). So west becomes south-east.
Why not the others: (A) turns clockwise. (C) turns only 45°. (D) turns 90° the wrong way.
Key point: Find the angle and sense of the turn from one pair, then check it with the second pair.

questions.sub_topic: Smallest prime greater than 90
questions.question: What is the smallest prime number greater than 90?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 97
Given: test the numbers after 90 that are odd.
Step 1: 91 = 7 × 13; 93 = 3 × 31; 95 = 5 × 19.
Step 2: 97 has no factor among 2, 3, 5 and 7 (√97 < 10), so it is prime.
Common mistake: taking 91 as prime; it looks prime but equals 7 × 13.

questions.sub_topic: Article on the President's power to pardon
questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India gives the President the power to grant pardons and to suspend, remit or commute sentences?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Article 72
Why: Article 72 gives the President the power of pardon, including in cases of a death sentence. (Article 161 gives Governors a similar but narrower power.)
Why not the others: (B) deals with the impeachment of the President. (C) is the power to issue ordinances. (D) deals with President's Rule in a state.
Key point: Only the President can pardon a death sentence.

questions.sub_topic: Trees in a row seventh from either end
questions.question: In a row of trees, one tree is 7th from either end. How many trees are there in the row?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 13
Answer steps: total = 7 + 7 − 1 = 13 (the tree itself is counted in both positions).
Why not the others: (A) counts the tree twice. (B) adds 1 instead of subtracting it. (C) subtracts 2.
Key point: Same item from both ends: total = left + right − 1.

questions.sub_topic: Principal from a compound-interest amount
questions.question: A sum of money becomes ₹13,310 in 3 years at 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually. What is the sum?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) ₹10,000
Given: A = ₹13,310, R = 10%, T = 3 years.
Step 1: A = P × (1.1)³ = 1.331P.
Step 2: P = 13,310 ÷ 1.331 = ₹10,000.
Common mistake: using simple interest (13,310 ÷ 1.3 ≈ ₹10,238, option A), or working back only one or two years (₹12,100 or ₹11,000, option C).

questions.sub_topic: Assertion and reason on two irrational numbers
questions.question:
Assertion (A): √2 is an irrational number.
Reason (R): π is an irrational number.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Answer steps: (A) is true: √2 cannot be written as p/q. (R) is true: π is also irrational (22/7 is only an approximation). But the fact that π is irrational says nothing about √2, so (R) does not explain (A).
Why not the others: (A) treats an unrelated fact as the reason. (C) and (D) call a true statement false.
Key point: Two true facts on the same topic are not necessarily cause and effect.

questions.sub_topic: Percentage rise in total use from February to May
questions.question:
Study the following table and answer the question that follows.

Electricity used (in kWh) by a housing society from January to June

| Month | Block A | Block B | Common areas |
|---|---|---|---|
| January | 1200 | 900 | 300 |
| February | 1000 | 800 | 200 |
| March | 1300 | 1000 | 300 |
| April | 1600 | 1400 | 400 |
| May | 2000 | 1800 | 500 |
| June | 1900 | 1700 | 400 |

Question: By what percentage did the society's total electricity use increase from February to May?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 115%
Given: February total = 1000 + 800 + 200 = 2000; May total = 2000 + 1800 + 500 = 4300.
Step 1: Increase = 4300 − 2000 = 2300.
Step 2: Percentage increase = 2300 ÷ 2000 × 100 = 115%.
Common mistake: dividing by the May figure (2300 ÷ 4300 ≈ 53.5%, option B), or giving May as a percentage of February (215%, option C).

questions.explanation:

questions.question:

|---|---|---|---|

| May | 2000 | 1800 | 500 |
| June | 1900 | 1700 | 400 |

Question: The society pays ₹7 per kWh for the first 2500 kWh used in a month and ₹9 per kWh for every kWh above 2500. What is its total bill for May?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) ₹33,700
Given: May total = 4300 kWh.
Step 1: First 2500 kWh at ₹7 = ₹17,500.
Step 2: Remaining 4300 − 2500 = 1800 kWh at ₹9 = ₹16,200.
Step 3: Bill = 17,500 + 16,200 = ₹33,700.
Common mistake: charging everything at ₹7 (₹30,100, option B) or at ₹9 (₹38,700, option C), or applying the two rates the wrong way round (2500 × 9 + 1800 × 7 = ₹35,100, option D).
